# Summary of Labour Party Manifesto 2005

The 2005 Labour Party Manifesto, titled "Britain Forward, Not Back," outlined the party's vision for a third term in government, building on what they characterized as significant achievements since 1997.

## Economic Foundation

Labour emphasized their economic record, highlighting the longest period of continuous growth in modern British history, low inflation, and the highest employment levels in 30 years. They pledged to maintain fiscal responsibility while continuing investment in public services. Key commitments included not raising basic or top income tax rates, raising the minimum wage, and pursuing full employment across all regions.

## Education Reform

Education remained the party's top priority. They promised personalized learning for every child, more specialist schools, and expanded academy programs. The manifesto committed to ensuring all children had access to quality education from primary through higher education, with a target of 50% of young people attending university by 2010.

## Healthcare Transformation

Labour pledged to continue transforming the NHS through sustained investment and reform. Key commitments included reducing maximum waiting times to 18 weeks from referral to treatment by 2008, offering patients choice of hospital, and tackling health inequalities. They promised to address MRSA infections and improve hospital cleanliness while expanding patient choice and control.

## Crime and Security

The manifesto promised neighborhood policing teams for every community, expanded police numbers, and continued crackdowns on antisocial behavior. On immigration, Labour proposed a points-based system for migrants and the introduction of ID cards backed by biometric data. Counter-terrorism measures included new control orders and enhanced powers for security agencies.

## Social Welfare

Labour committed to ending child poverty by 2020, starting with halving it by 2010. They promised universal affordable childcare, extended paid maternity leave to nine months, and continued support for pensioners through Pension Credit. The manifesto also pledged to increase homeownership by another one to two million.

## International Affairs

Labour emphasized Britain's role in Europe and international leadership on climate change and African development. They committed to a referendum on the EU Constitutional Treaty, continued support for NATO, and achieving the UN aid target of 0.7% of national income by 2013. The manifesto defended the Iraq war while acknowledging public disagreement.

## Constitutional Reform

The party promised to complete House of Lords reform, devolve more power to local authorities and communities, and strengthen local government through reduced bureaucracy and greater freedoms. They also pledged to support the 2012 London Olympics bid and continue investing in arts, culture, and sport.

The manifesto positioned Labour as the party of stability and progress, contrasting their record with what they characterized as Conservative failures of the past.
